questions.q: A source of frequency ν gives 6 beats/second when sounded with a source of frequency 200 Hz. The second Harmonic of frequency 2ν of the source gives 8 beats/second when sounded with a source of frequency 420 Hz. The value of ν is
questions.explanation: ν = 200±6, so ν = 194 or 206. Also 2ν = 420±8, so ν = 214 or 206. The common value satisfying both is ν = 206 Hz.

questions.q: The angle between the particle velocity and wave velocity in a transverse wave is [except when the particle passes through the mean position]
questions.explanation: In a transverse wave the medium particles oscillate perpendicular to the direction of wave travel, so the particle velocity is always at 90° ($\pi/2$) to the wave velocity.

questions.q: A motor-cyclist moving towards a huge cliff with a speed of 18 kmh$^{-1}$, blows a horn of source frequency 325 Hz. If the speed of sound in air is 330 ms$^{-1}$, the number of beats heard by him is
questions.explanation: The reflected frequency is $f''=f\dfrac{V+V_s}{V-V_s}$; with $V_s=5\,ms^{-1}$, $V=330\,ms^{-1}$, the beats $=f''-f=\dfrac{325\times2\times5}{325}=10$.

questions.q: To propagate both longitudinal and transverse waves, a material must have
questions.note: The standard answer should be (A) bulk and shear moduli, since propagating a transverse wave requires shear (rigidity) elasticity, not Young's modulus, which governs longitudinal stretching of a rod rather than wave propagation in a bulk medium.
questions.explanation: Longitudinal waves need bulk (volume) elasticity and transverse waves need shear (rigidity) elasticity; the reasoning suggests option (A) (bulk and shear moduli), but the KEA key marks (D), Young's and Bulk modulus, as correct (as per KEA key).

questions.q: The equation of a stationary wave is $y = 2\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{15}\right)\cos(48\pi t)$. The distance between a node and its next antinode is
questions.explanation: Wave number $k=\pi/15 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2\pi/k = 30$ units; the node-to-next-antinode distance is $\lambda/4 = 7.5$ units.

questions.q: First overtone frequency of a closed pipe of length '$l_1$' is equal to the 2$^{nd}$ harmonic frequency of an open pipe of length '$l_2$'. The ratio $\dfrac{l_1}{l_2}$ =
questions.explanation: First overtone of closed pipe = 3v/4$l_1$; 2nd harmonic of open pipe = 2v/2$l_2$ = v/$l_2$. Equating: 3v/4$l_1$ = v/$l_2$ ⟹ $l_1$/$l_2$ = 3/4.

questions.q: The waves set up in a closed pipe are
questions.explanation: Sound waves in a closed pipe are longitudinal, and superposition of incident and reflected waves forms stationary (standing) waves.

questions.q: A source of sound is moving with a velocity of 50 ms$^{-1}$ towards a stationary observer. The observer measures the frequency of sound as 500 Hz. The apparent frequency of sound as heard by the observer when source is moving away from him with the same speed is (Speed of sound at room temperature 350 ms$^{-1}$)
questions.explanation: Approaching: $500=f_0\dfrac{350}{350-50}=f_0\dfrac{7}{6}\Rightarrow f_0=428.6$ Hz. Receding: $f'=f_0\dfrac{350}{350+50}=428.6\times\dfrac{7}{8}\approx375$ Hz.

questions.q: When two tuning forks A and B are sounded together, 4 beats per second are heard. The frequency of the fork B is 384 Hz. When one of the prongs of the fork A is filed and sounded with B, the beat frequency increases, then the frequency of the fork A is
questions.explanation: Filing a tuning fork's prongs increases its frequency. Since the beat frequency increased after filing, A's original frequency must have been above B's, i.e. 384+4=388 Hz, so filing moves it further from 384 Hz.

questions.q: A stretched string is vibrating in the second overtone, then the number of nodes and antinodes between the ends of the string are respectively
questions.explanation: The second overtone is the third harmonic (3 loops), which has 4 nodes and 3 antinodes.

questions.q: A metallic wire of 1 m length has a mass of 10 \times 10^{-3} kg. If a tension of 100 N is applied to a wire, what is the speed of transverse wave?

A train is approaching towards a platform with a speed of 10 ms$^{-1}$ while blowing a whistle of frequency 340 Hz. What is the frequency of whistle heard by a stationary observer on the platform? Given speed of sound = 340 ms$^{-1}$.
questions.explanation: f' = f\times v/(v-v_s) = 340\times340/330 \approx 350 Hz.

questions.q: A pipe of 30 cm long and open at both the ends produces harmonics. Which harmonic mode of pipe resonates a 1.1 kHz source? Given speed of sound in air = 330 ms$^{-1}$.
questions.explanation: Fundamental frequency f$_1$ = v/2L = 330/0.6 = 550 Hz; 1100 Hz = 2\times550 Hz, i.e. the second harmonic (all harmonics allowed in an open pipe).

questions.q: The equation of a transverse wave is given by y = 0.05 sin $\pi$(2t $-$ 0.02x), where x, y are in metre and t is in second. The minimum distance of separation between two particles which are in phase and the wave velocity are respectively
questions.explanation: Comparing with $y=A\sin(\omega t-kx)$: $\omega=2\pi$ rad/s, $k=0.02\pi$ rad/m. Wavelength (the least separation between particles in the same phase) $\lambda=2\pi/k=100$ m; wave speed $v=\omega/k=100\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.

questions.q: The frequency of the second overtone of the open pipe is equal to the frequency of the first overtone of the closed pipe. The ratio of the lengths of the open pipe and the closed pipe is
questions.explanation: Open pipe 2nd overtone (3rd harmonic): $f=3v/2L_o$. Closed pipe 1st overtone (3rd harmonic): $f=3v/4L_c$. Equating gives $L_o:L_c=2:1$.

questions.q: A person with vibrating tuning fork of frequency 338 Hz is moving towards a vertical wall with a speed of 2 ms$^{-1}$. Velocity of sound in air is 340 ms$^{-1}$. The number of beats heard by that person per second is
questions.explanation: The wall receives sound from a source (the person) approaching at 2 ms$^{-1}$: $f'=f\dfrac{v}{v-v_s}=338\times\dfrac{340}{338}=340$ Hz. The person (now a moving observer approaching the wall) hears this reflected wave as $f''=f'\dfrac{v+v_o}{v}=340\times\dfrac{342}{340}=342$ Hz. Beats $=f''-f=342-338=4$.

questions.q: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: If the wave is longitudinal, it must be a mechanical wave.
If the wave is mechanical, it may OR may not be a transverse wave.
Mechanical waves cannot propagate in vacuum.
'Diffraction' helps us to distinguish between sound wave and light wave.
questions.explanation: Both sound and light waves diffract, so diffraction cannot be used to distinguish between them; the other three statements are correct.

questions.q: Intensity level of sound whose intensity is 10$^{-8}$ Wm$^{-2}$ is ..... dB
The equation of a wave is given by $y = 10\,Sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{45}t + \alpha\right)$. If the displacement is 5 cm at $t=0$, then the total phase at $t = 7.5$ sec. is .................
questions.explanation: At $t=0$: $10\sin\alpha=5 \Rightarrow \alpha=\pi/6$. Total phase at $t=7.5$: $\dfrac{2\pi}{45}(7.5)+\alpha=\pi/3+\pi/6=\pi/2$.

questions.q: Two tuning forks, $A$ and $B$, produce notes of frequencies 258 Hz and 262 Hz. An unknown note sounded with $A$ produces certain beats. When the same note is sounded with $B$, the beat frequency gets doubled. The unknown frequency is .....................
questions.explanation: Let unknown frequency be $x<258$: beats with $A$ = $258-x$, beats with $B$ = $262-x = 2(258-x)$, solving gives $x=254$ Hz.

questions.q: A wire under tension vibrates with a fundamental frequency of 600 Hz. If the length of the wire is doubled, the radius is halved and the wire is made to vibrate under one-ninth the tension. Then the fundamental frequency will become .......................
questions.explanation: $f \propto \dfrac{1}{Lr}\sqrt{T}$ (since $\mu\propto r^2$); $f_2/f_1=(1/2)(2)\sqrt{1/9}=1/3$, so $f_2=600/3=200$ Hz.

questions.q: A bat flies at a steady speed of 4 ms$^{-1}$ emitting a sound of $f=90\times10^3$ Hz. It is flying horizontally towards a vertical wall. The frequency of the reflected sound as detected by the bat will be ..................... (Take velocity of sound in air as 330 ms$^{-1}$).
questions.explanation: The wall (stationary reflector) receives $f'=f\dfrac{v}{v-v_{bat}}$ and re-emits it; the bat (moving observer) then hears $f''=f'\dfrac{v+v_{bat}}{v}=90\times10^3\times\dfrac{334}{326}\approx92.1\times10^3$ Hz.

questions.q: A closed organ pipe and an open organ pipe of same length produce 2 beats/second while vibrating in their fundamental modes. The length of the open organ pipe is halved and that of closed pipe is doubled. Then, the number of beats produced per second while vibrating in the fundamental mode is .....................
questions.explanation: Initially $f_{open}-f_{closed}=v/4L=2$ Hz. After halving the open pipe's length and doubling the closed pipe's length: $f_{open}'=v/L=8$ Hz, $f_{closed}'=v/8L=1$ Hz; new beat frequency $=8-1=7$ Hz.

questions.q: A uniform wire of length $L$, diameter $D$ and density $P$ is stretched under a tension $T$. The correct relation between its fundamental frequency 'f', the length $L$ and the diameter $D$ is .....................
questions.explanation: $f=\dfrac{1}{2L}\sqrt{T/\mu}$ with $\mu\propto D^2$, so $f\propto\dfrac{1}{LD}$.

questions.q: Sound waves transfer
questions.explanation: A sound wave carries energy from source to receiver and also transfers momentum (which is why sound can exert radiation pressure).

questions.q: A stationary point source of sound emits sound uniformly in all directions in a non-absorbing medium. Two points P and Q are at a distance of 4 m and 9 m respectively from the source. The ratio of amplitudes of the waves at P & Q is
questions.explanation: Since intensity $\propto 1/r^2$ and amplitude $\propto 1/r$, the ratio $A_P/A_Q = r_Q/r_P = 9/4$.

questions.q: $y = 3\sin\pi\left(\dfrac{t}{2}-\dfrac{x}{4}\right)$ represents an equation of a progressive wave, where 't' is in second and 'x' is in metre. The distance travelled by the wave in 5 seconds is
questions.explanation: Comparing with $y=A\sin(\omega t-kx)$: $\omega=\pi/2,\,k=\pi/4$, so $v=\omega/k=2\ \text{ms}^{-1}$; distance in 5 s $=2\times5=10$ m.

questions.q: A cylindrical tube open at both the ends has a fundamental frequency of 390 Hz in air. If $1/4^{th}$ of the tube is immersed vertically in water the fundamental frequency of air column is
questions.explanation: Open-open tube: $f_0=v/2L=390$. With $1/4$ submerged, the remaining length $3L/4$ acts as a closed-open tube: $f'=v/4(3L/4)=v/3L=(2Lf_0)/3L=2f_0/3=260$ Hz.
